strategy.summary: The todo app (public/app.js, in-memory per page) lets users tick todos to complete them, filter All/Active/Completed and clear completed todos. Playwright e2e tests against the real static server prove the strike-through and items-left count, each filter's contents and pressed state, and the visibility and effect of "Clear completed".
inScope: Completing and uncompleting a todo via its checkbox (strike-through, items-left count)
All / Active / Completed filters and their aria-pressed state
Clear completed button visibility and effect
outOfScope: Persistence across reloads (the app keeps todos in memory only; ticket doesn't ask for it)
assumptions: The app's only server is server.js serving static files; it runs for real via Playwright's existing webServer config. Nothing is faked.
Todos live in page memory, so each test gets fresh state from its own page; no cleanup is needed.
'Struck through' is checked as the computed text-decoration-line of the todo's title (line-through), which the app's stylesheet applies to li.completed span.
'Shown as pressed' means aria-pressed="true" on the selected filter button and "false" on the others, as app.js sets it.
openQuestions: The #count element has no role or test id; tests locate it by id. Consider adding data-testid or role="status".

risks.description: Count wording regression (e.g. '1 items left') or off-by-one in the count
risks.mitigation: Exact-text assertions on the count element in TC1, TC2, TC7

risks.description: Filter shows wrong subset or loses order
risks.mitigation: TC3–TC5 assert the full ordered list of titles per filter

risks.description: Clear completed removes active todos or stays visible
risks.mitigation: TC6, TC7 assert visibility and the remaining todos

acceptanceCriteria.text: Ticking a todo's checkbox marks it completed: its title is struck through and the items-left count goes down by one; unticking reverses both.
Active shows only non-completed todos, Completed only completed ones, All every todo; the selected filter is shown as pressed.
"Clear completed" is visible only while at least one todo is completed, and clicking it removes every completed todo.

testCases.title: ticking a todo strikes it through and decrements the items left
preconditions: App open with todos 'Walk dog', 'Pay rent' added
testCases.expected: Checkbox is checked, 'Walk dog' title has line-through, 'Pay rent' does not; count reads '1 item left' (was '2 items left')

testCases.title: unticking a completed todo removes the strike-through and restores the items left
preconditions: Todos 'Walk dog', 'Pay rent' added, 'Walk dog' ticked
testCases.expected: Checkbox unchecked, title text-decoration not line-through, count reads '2 items left'

testCases.title: Active filter shows only todos that are not completed and is pressed
preconditions: Todos 'Walk dog', 'Pay rent', 'Call mum' added, 'Pay rent' ticked
testCases.expected: List titles are exactly ['Walk dog', 'Call mum']; Active aria-pressed=true, All and Completed false

testCases.title: Completed filter shows only completed todos and is pressed
testCases.expected: List titles exactly ['Pay rent']; Completed pressed, others not

testCases.title: All filter shows every todo in order after another filter and is pressed
preconditions: Same three todos, 'Pay rent' ticked, Completed filter selected
testCases.expected: List titles exactly ['Walk dog', 'Pay rent', 'Call mum']; All pressed, others not
testCases.rationale: Returning to All restores the full list

testCases.title: ticking a todo under the Active filter removes it from the view
preconditions: Todos 'Walk dog', 'Pay rent' added, Active filter selected
testCases.expected: List titles exactly ['Pay rent']; count '1 item left'

testCases.title: Clear completed is hidden until a todo is completed and hides again when it is unticked
testCases.expected: Hidden with the todo listed; visible after tick; hidden after untick

testCases.title: Clear completed removes every completed todo and keeps the active ones
preconditions: Todos 'Walk dog', 'Pay rent', 'Call mum', 'Buy bread' added; 'Walk dog' and 'Call mum' ticked
testCases.expected: List titles exactly ['Pay rent', 'Buy bread']; count '2 items left'; Clear completed hidden
testCases.rationale: Removes all (not just one) completed todos

strategy.environmentNotes: Playwright's webServer starts `node server.js` on 4173 (BASE_URL http://localhost:4173). No env vars or seed data.

review.standard: Playwright rules: never use CSS selectors; General: avoid brittle selectors that rely on DOM structure
review.summary: `todoTitles` finds each todo's title with the CSS tag selector `.locator('span')`, so it depends on app.js wrapping the title in a <span>, when the list item's own text is already exactly the title.
review.failureScenario:
Say app.js renders the title as the label's text node, or in a or

, instead of a . Todos still add, filter and clear correctly. But `todoTitles` then matches nothing, so `addTodos` (line 21) and the list assertions in TC3, TC4, TC5, TC6 and TC8 (lines 59, 69, 80, 90, 117) fail even though the app works. `todoList(page).getByRole('listitem')` with `toHaveText(titles)` checks the same ordered titles, as tests/add-todo.spec.js already does. That works because the checkbox in each item adds no text.
review.response: The e2e standards forbid text checks on a row/group locator (toHaveText on a list item passes when the words are anywhere in it, and TestForge refuses publishing over it). The <span> is the one element that shows the title and the app offers no role or test id for it; a follow-up asks for a data-testid on it.
